1. In the OCI Console, go to Networking > Virtual Cloud Networks and select your VCN
2. Under Resources, click Security Lists and open the list attached to the affected subnet
3. In Ingress Rules, locate any rule with Source CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 that allows TCP port 3389 or All Protocols
4. Delete that rule, or edit it so Source CIDR is a restricted range (e.g., your IP) and Destination Port is 3389 only
5. Click Save Changes

fields.title: Security list restricts ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22 (SSH)
fields.remediation_text: Restrict **SSH** to trusted sources using least-privilege network rules; avoid `0.0.0.0/0`. Prefer **private access** via VPN/peering or a hardened **bastion**. Apply **network segmentation** (NSGs/security lists) to narrow scope. Enforce **key-based authentication**, disable password login, and monitor access.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Networking > Virtual Cloud Networks and open your VCN
2. Click Security Lists, then select <example_resource_name>
3. In Ingress Rules, locate any rule with Source CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 and Protocol TCP (or All) that includes port 22
4. Edit the rule: change Source CIDR to a specific allowed range (e.g., your office IP/CIDR) and set Destination Port Range to 22, or delete the rule
5. Click Save changes

fields.title: Subnet has VCN flow logging enabled
fields.remediation_text: Enable **VCN flow logs** for all subnets-prefer VCN-wide enablement for complete coverage-and route to centralized log groups. Enforce least privilege on log access, set retention, and integrate with a SIEM. Use `capture filters` and `sampling` to control volume. Review logs to support defense-in-depth.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Networking > Flow logs
2. Click Enable flow logs
3. Select a Log group (or create one) and a Capture filter (or create one)
4. Click Next, then Add enablement points
5. Choose Virtual cloud network and select your VCN (or choose Subnet and select the subnet)
6. Click Add enablement points, then Next, then Enable flow logs

fields.title: Object Storage bucket is encrypted with a Customer Managed Key (CMK)
fields.remediation_text: Encrypt buckets with `CMEK`. Apply **least privilege** to key usage, enforce **separation of duties** between key and storage admins, mandate regular rotation, and monitor key access. Use **defense in depth** so encryption complements strict IAM and network controls rather than replacing them.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Storage > Object Storage & Archive Storage > Buckets
3. Open the target bucket
4. Click Edit bucket
5. Under Encryption, select Customer-managed key and choose the desired Vault key
6. Click Save

fields.title: Object Storage bucket has write-level logging enabled
fields.remediation_text:
Enable `write` service logs on all buckets and route them to a centralized log group for monitoring.

Apply **least privilege** to log data, enforce retention and immutability, and alert on anomalous write activity. Use **defense in depth** so bucket changes are accountable and swiftly detected.
fields.remediation_cli: oci logging log create --log-group-id <log-group-ocid> --display-name ObjectStorage-Write-Logs --log-type SERVICE --configuration '{"compartmentId":"<compartment-ocid>","source":{"service":"objectstorage","resource":"<bucket-name>","category":"write","sourceType":"OCISERVICE"}}'
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, select the target region and go to Observability & Management > Logging > Log groups
2. Open an existing log group or click Create log group
3. Click Create log
4. Type: Service
5. Service: Object Storage
6. Category: write
7. Resource: select the target bucket (bucket name must match)
8. Ensure Enabled is checked
9. Click Create

fields.title: Object Storage bucket is not publicly accessible
fields.remediation_text: Keep buckets **private** (`NoPublicAccess`) under the **least privilege** principle. For external sharing, use **pre-authenticated requests** or signed URLs with scoped permissions and expiry. Restrict access via IAM policies, enforce guardrails (*e.g.*, Security Zones), and regularly review bucket visibility.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Object Storage > Buckets and open <bucket-name>
3. Click Edit (Bucket details)
4. Set Public access type to "No public access"
5. Click Save

fields.title: Object Storage bucket has versioning enabled
fields.remediation_text: Enable **bucket versioning** (`Enabled`) for data that needs recovery. Apply **least privilege** to delete and overwrite actions, use **retention rules** or legal holds for critical data, and add **lifecycle policies** to manage older versions-providing **defense in depth** against destructive changes.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Storage > Buckets and open the target bucket
3. In Bucket details, find Versioning and click Edit
4. Select Enabled and click Save

fields.title: Tenancy admins are not used for routine operations
fields.remediation_text: Use least-privileged identities for routine work; reserve admins for approved break-glass.

fields.title: Tenancy-admin privileges are limited to the approved admin population
fields.remediation_text: Remove admin privileges from users outside the approved population.

fields.title: Storage resources are encrypted at rest
fields.remediation_text: No action required.

fields.title: OCI databases have automatic backups / point-in-time recovery
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.

fields.title: OCI databases are encrypted at rest
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: No action required; consider a customer-managed key.

fields.title: Mail domains publish DKIM records
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Publish the DKIM TXT/CNAME record supplied by the mail provider.

fields.title: Mail domains in OCI DNS publish SPF and DMARC
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Add TXT records 'v=spf1 ... -all' at the apex and 'v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; ...' at _dmarc.

fields.title: Public DNS zones have DNSSEC enabled
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Enable DNSSEC on the zone.

fields.title: Dynamic group matching rules are scoped
fields.message: TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
fields.remediation_text: Add a compartment or tag condition to the matching rule.

fields.title: No public (any-user) or cross-tenancy IAM grants
fields.remediation_text: Remove or scope the statement.

fields.title: IAM policies avoid any-user and wildcard administrator grants
fields.remediation_text: Replace the statement with least-privilege grants scoped to a compartment.

fields.title: No active IAM user is inactive for more than 90 days
fields.remediation_text: Disable or delete inactive users.

fields.title: Vault keys are enabled, rotating and owned
fields.remediation_text: Enable rotation and tag the key with an owner.

fields.title: Public load balancers expose HTTPS only
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Add an SSL configuration to listeners or replace HTTP listeners with an HTTPS redirect rule set.

fields.title: Load balancers have access/error logs enabled
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Enable access and error logs for the load balancer.

fields.title: Load balancer TLS listeners use TLS 1.2+ and modern ciphers
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Use a custom SSL cipher suite and protocols TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3 on every TLS listener.

fields.title: Log archive buckets are immutable (locked retention rule)
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Add a retention rule and lock it.

fields.title: Security logs are retained for at least 12 months
fields.remediation_text: Export logs through Service Connector Hub to a bucket with a >=365-day retention rule.

fields.title: Internet-facing VCNs have an OCI Network Firewall (IPS)
fields.remediation_text: Deploy an OCI Network Firewall with an IPS policy in the VCN's region.

fields.title: Database ports are not exposed to the internet
fields.remediation_text: Restrict database ingress to private CIDRs.

fields.title: No unapproved internet ingress in security lists / NSGs
fields.remediation_text: Restrict the source CIDR or remove the rule.

fields.title: Compute instances are registered and patched in OS Management Hub
fields.remediation_text: Register the instance and apply pending updates.

fields.title: Privileged users have MFA enabled
fields.remediation_text: Enable MFA for every privileged user.

fields.title: A tenancy-wide resource inventory can be produced
fields.remediation_text: Grant the assessment user inspect access via the Search service.

fields.title: Block and boot volumes have a backup policy assigned
fields.remediation_text: Assign a backup policy (bronze/silver/gold or a custom policy) to every volume.

fields.title: Host vulnerabilities are severity-classified
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Review unclassified findings.

fields.title: Compute instances are covered by a Vulnerability Scanning host scan target
fields.remediation_text: Create a host scan recipe and a host scan target covering the compartment of each instance.
fields.remediation_cli: oci vulnerability-scanning host scan target create --compartment-id <C> --host-scan-recipe-id <R> --target-compartment-id <C>

fields.title: Instances were vulnerability-scanned recently
fields.remediation_text: Schedule a recurring host scan recipe.

fields.title: Public load balancers are protected by an OCI WAF
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Create a WAF policy and a web application firewall for each public load balancer.

fields.title: Oracle Analytics Cloud instance is deployed within a Virtual Cloud Network or restricts public access to allowed sources
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Prefer **private deployment in a VCN** and apply **least privilege** network access. *If public is required*, enforce **allowlists** to specific IPs/CIDRs and never include `0.0.0.0/0`. Use **private access channels/service gateways**, require **MFA/SSO**, and apply **defense in depth** (WAF, audit monitoring) to reduce exposure.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Analytics & AI > Analytics Cloud and select your instance
2. On Instance Details, under Network Access, click Edit next to Access Control
3. Remove any 0.0.0.0/0 entry (if present)
4. Add an access rule with the specific allowed public IP or CIDR
5. Click Save

fields.title: Tenancy audit log retention period is 365 days or greater
fields.remediation_text:
Set audit retention to `>= 365` days at the tenancy level and protect the setting with **least privilege** and **separation of duties**.

Adopt **defense in depth**: export audit logs to centralized, immutable storage or a SIEM for extended retention, integrity, and continuous monitoring.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Open the OCI Console and go to Governance & Administration > Audit
2. Click Configuration
3. Set Retention period (days) to 365
4. Click Save

fields.title: Block volume is encrypted with a Customer Managed Key (CMK)
fields.remediation_text:
Use **Customer-Managed Keys** in Vault for all block volumes.
- Enforce least privilege and separation of duties on key usage
- Rotate keys regularly and monitor KMS events
- Validate that key disable/deny revokes data access
Apply the same controls to snapshots and backups.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Block Storage > Block Volumes
2. Open the failing volume
3. Click Edit
4. Under Encryption, select "Encrypt using customer-managed keys" and choose the vault key
5. Click Save changes

fields.title: Boot volume is encrypted with Customer Managed Key
fields.remediation_text: Encrypt boot volumes with **customer-managed keys** and enforce **least privilege** on key usage. Define a key lifecycle (new keys for rotation), monitor and audit key access, and restrict key scope to required compartments and services to achieve **defense in depth** and rapid revocation when needed.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Storage > Block Storage > Boot Volumes
2. Click the boot volume name
3. Click Edit (or Assign master encryption key)
4. Select a Customer-managed key from Vault
5. Click Save

fields.title: Cloud Guard is enabled in the root compartment of the tenancy
fields.remediation_text: Enable **Cloud Guard** at the tenancy root to centralize monitoring and automated response. Apply **defense in depth** by using detectors/responders, integrate alerts with monitoring, and enforce **least privilege** for its roles. Regularly tune policies and review findings to prevent blind spots.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Security > Cloud Guard
2. Ensure the root compartment is selected
3. Click Enable Cloud Guard
4. Choose a Reporting region
5. Click Enable

fields.title: Compute instance has in-transit encryption enabled
fields.remediation_text: Enable **in-transit encryption** for all paravirtualized volume attachments and make it standard in golden images and IaC. Apply **defense in depth** with **customer-managed keys** and regular rotation. Periodically verify attachments and remediate drift so no instance communicates with volumes over unencrypted channels.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Compute > Instances and open the target instance
2. Under Resources, click the boot volume attachment, choose Edit, enable "Use in-transit encryption", and Save
3. For each attached block volume (paravirtualized), open the attachment (More actions > Edit), enable "Use in-transit encryption", and Save
4. If Edit isn't available for an attachment, detach it and reattach it with "Use in-transit encryption" checked

fields.title: Compute instance legacy metadata service endpoint is disabled
fields.remediation_text: Disable **IMDS v1** and require **IMDS v2** across all instances. Migrate applications to session-authorized requests and confirm image support. Enforce **least privilege** for instance principals, restrict untrusted processes from reaching `169.254.169.254`, and monitor metadata access to provide **defense in depth**.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Compute > Instances
2. Select <example_resource_name>
3. In Instance Details, next to Instance metadata service, click Edit
4. Set Allowed IMDS version to Version 2 only
5. Click Save changes

fields.title: Compute instance has Secure Boot enabled
fields.remediation_text: Enable **Secure Boot** across instances and prefer **shielded instances**. Pair with **TPM** and **Measured Boot** where supported for defense in depth. Permit only trusted, signed kernels and drivers, and manage updates via hardened golden images and code signing. *On Windows VMs, use Secure Boot with TPM and Measured Boot.*
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Compute > Instances
2. Click Create instance
3. Choose an image and shape that support Shielded instance
4. In the Security section, click Edit under Shielded instance and enable Secure Boot
5. Click Create
6. To remove the failing resource, select the original non-shielded instance > More actions > Terminate

fields.title: Autonomous Shared Database (ADB) is deployed within a VCN or restricts public access with whitelisted IPs excluding 0.0.0.0/0
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text:
Prefer **VCN private endpoints** to eliminate internet exposure. If public access is required, enforce **least privilege** by limiting ACLs to specific CIDRs or VCNs; never use `0.0.0.0/0`.

Add **defense in depth** with NSGs and private connectivity (VPN/peering), monitor access, and rotate client wallets regularly.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Autonomous Database and select the instance
2. Click More Actions > Update
3. Under Network Access, enable Access control list (ACL)
4. Add an allowed IP/CIDR (exclude 0.0.0.0/0) and remove any 0.0.0.0/0 entry
5. Click Save

fields.title: Tenancy has at least one notification topic with active subscriptions
fields.remediation_text: Create a centralized **Notifications** topic with one or more **subscriptions**, and route critical Events/monitoring to it. Apply **least privilege** to topic management, use redundant channels, test delivery regularly, and tune filters to reduce noise. *Consider* escalation paths for `critical` alerts.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Menu > Application Integration > Notifications > Topics
2. Click Create Topic, enter a name, and click Create
3. Open the topic, click Create Subscription
4. Select a protocol (e.g., Function), choose/provide the endpoint, and click Create
5. Verify the subscription lifecycle state shows Active (confirm if prompted for protocols like Email)

fields.title: Event rule monitoring Cloud Guard problems has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Implement **event-driven alerts** for Cloud Guard problem lifecycle events and route them to trusted **notification channels** and your **SOC/SIEM**. Enforce **least privilege** on publish/subscribe, align rules with the **reporting region**, and use **severity-based filtering** to prioritize response within a **defense-in-depth** approach.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Menu > Application Integration > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create Rule and select the Compartment; switch to the Cloud Guard reporting Region
3. In Conditions, add event types: com.oraclecloud.cloudguard.problemdetected, com.oraclecloud.cloudguard.problemdismissed, com.oraclecloud.cloudguard.problemremediated
4. Under Actions, add Notifications and select the desired Topic
5. Ensure the rule is Enabled and click Create

fields.title: Event rule monitoring IAM group changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Create **Events rules** for IAM group `create`, `update`, and `delete` and route them to **Notifications** channels consumed by the SOC. Enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties** on rules/topics, forward events to a **SIEM**, and periodically test alert delivery.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule and set Name
3. In Condition, select Event types and add:
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.creategroup
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletegroup
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updategroup
4. In Actions, add Notifications and select an existing Topic
5. Click Create to save the rule

fields.title: Event rule monitoring IAM policy changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Create OCI Events rules for `...createpolicy`, `...updatepolicy`, and `...deletepolicy` with a **notification action** to trusted channels. Enforce **least privilege** on IAM and Events administration, require change approvals, and routinely test alerting to ensure rapid detection.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service
2. Click Create Rule and set Display Name (leave Enabled)
3. Under Conditions, choose Event Type, set Service Name to Identity and Access Management, and select:
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createpolicy
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletepolicy
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updatepolicy
4. Under Actions, select Action Type: Notifications, then choose the target Topic
5. Click Create

fields.title: Event rule for identity provider changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Configure rules to capture **identity provider** `create`, `update`, and `delete` events and send notifications to responders and SIEM. Enforce **least privilege** on IdP management, require approvals for changes, and test alert paths. Use **defense in depth** with audit logging to spot anomalous identity changes.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules and click Create rule
2. Set Name and select the target Compartment
3. In Rule condition, add event types: CreateIdentityProvider, DeleteIdentityProvider, UpdateIdentityProvider (service: Identity)
4. In Actions, add Notification, select your Topic
5. Ensure Enabled is On and click Create

fields.title: Event rule for IdP group mapping changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Define **Events rules** for IdP group mapping changes (`com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.addidpgroupmapping`, `...removeidpgroupmapping`, `...updateidpgroupmapping`) and route notifications to monitored channels via **OCI Notifications**. Apply **least privilege** and **separation of duties**, and integrate alerts with a SIEM for **defense in depth**.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule
3. Condition: add Event types:
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.addidpgroupmapping
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.removeidpgroupmapping
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateidpgroupmapping
4. Actions: Add action > Notifications (ONS) and select the target Topic
5. Ensure Rule is Enabled and click Create

fields.title: Event rule monitoring local OCI user authentication has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Create an Events rule for `com.oraclecloud.identitysignon.interactivelogin` with **notification actions** delivering real-time alerts to monitored channels or workflows. Integrate with a SIEM, tune filters to reduce noise, and apply **least privilege** and **defense in depth** to limit local account exposure.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Application Integration > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule
3. Set Name and select the target Compartment
4. In Condition, set Event Type to: com.oraclecloud.identitysignon.interactivelogin
5. Add Action: choose Notifications, select the Topic, and ensure it is Enabled
6. Click Create

fields.title: Event rule monitoring network gateway changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text:
Define **event rules** that match `create`, `update`, `delete`, `attach`, and `detach` actions for all gateway types and send **notifications** to monitored channels.

Apply **least privilege** on topics, cover all compartments/regions, integrate with SIEM, and use **defense in depth** with network change approvals.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule and select the target Compartment
3. Set Display name
4. Under Matching events, add these Event types:
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createdrg
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletedrg
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatedrg
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createdrgattachment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletedrgattachment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatedrgattachment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changeinternetgatewaycompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createinternetgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deleteinternetgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updateinternetgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changelocalpeeringgatewaycompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createlocalpeeringgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletelocalpeeringgateway.end
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatelocalpeeringgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.natgateway.changenatgatewaycompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.natgateway.createnatgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.natgateway.deletenatgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.natgateway.updatenatgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.attachserviceid
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.changeservicegatewaycompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.createservicegateway
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.deleteservicegateway.end
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.detachserviceid
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.updateservicegateway
5. Add action: Notification, select the target Notifications (ONS) topic
6. Click Create (ensure the rule is enabled)

fields.title: Event rule monitoring network security group changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text:
Implement **Events** rules for NSG lifecycle changes with **notification actions** to a monitored topic/SIEM.
- Include `createnetworksecuritygroup`, `updatenetworksecuritygroup`, `deletenetworksecuritygroup`, `changenetworksecuritygroupcompartment`
- Enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties** on NSG and Events admins
- Regularly test and tune alerts
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule
3. Set Display name and Compartment
4. Under Conditions, add Event types:
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changenetworksecuritygroupcompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createnetworksecuritygroup
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletenetworksecuritygroup
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatenetworksecuritygroup
5. Under Actions, click Add action > Notifications, select Publish to topic, choose the ONS topic
6. Click Create to save the rule

fields.title: Event rule for route table changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Create an **Events rule** that captures route table `create`, `update`, `delete`, and `changeCompartment` events and routes them to **notifications** used by on-call and SIEM. Enforce **least privilege** on route edits, require **change approvals**, and apply **defense in depth** with auditing and automated response.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules.
2. Click Create rule and select the target Compartment; set a Display name.
3. In Condition, add event types:
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changeroutetablecompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createroutetable
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deleteroutetable
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updateroutetable
4. In Actions, add Notifications (ONS) and select the desired Topic.
5. Ensure the rule is Enabled and click Create.

fields.title: Event rule monitoring security list changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Define **Events** rules for security list create/update/delete and route them to **Notifications** or automated responders. Enforce **least privilege** for network and Events admins, apply **change control** with logging, cover critical compartments/regions, and periodically test alerts for reliability.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule, set a name and compartment
3. In Condition, set Event Type to include exactly:
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changesecuritylistcompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createsecuritylist
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletesecuritylist
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatesecuritylist
4. Click Add action, choose Notifications, select an existing topic
5. Ensure the action is enabled and click Create

fields.title: Event rule monitoring user changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text:
Create and maintain **Events rules** for IAM user lifecycle changes and attach reliable **notification actions** to security-owned channels (SIEM, paging, email, chat).

Enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties** on rule management, and use **defense in depth** by correlating alerts with audit logs and automating containment.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules and click Create Rule
2. Select the Compartment and enter a Name
3. Under Rule Conditions, set Event Type to include:
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createuser
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deleteuser
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateuser
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateusercapabilities
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateuserstate
4. Under Actions, add a Notification action and select the desired Notifications (ONS) Topic
5. Click Create

fields.title: Event rule monitoring VCN changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text:
Create and enable **Events rules** for VCN lifecycle changes (**create**, **update**, **delete**) with **notification actions** to monitored channels.

Apply **least privilege** to manage rules and notifications, integrate alerts with incident response, and periodically test to support **defense in depth**.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule and enter a name; set Rule state to Enabled
3. Under Conditions, add Event types: com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createvcn, com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletevcn, com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatevcn
4. Under Actions, add Notification and select the target Notifications topic
5. Click Create to save the rule

fields.title: File Storage file system is encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Encrypt file systems with **Customer-Managed Keys** in OCI KMS. Apply **least privilege** on key usage, enable periodic rotation, and require dual control for key administration. Monitor key activity with centralized logging. Use **defense in depth** by combining `CMEK` with network isolation and strong access governance.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Storage > File Storage > File Systems and select the target file system
3. In the Encryption section, click Edit (or Change key)
4. Select Customer-managed key, choose the Vault and KMS key
5. Click Save to apply

fields.title: All IAM policies granting manage/use on groups or users in the tenancy restrict access to the Administrators group
fields.remediation_text: Apply **least privilege**: avoid tenancy-wide manage/use on groups or users. When delegation is required, include a condition excluding the **Administrators** group (e.g., `target.group.name != 'Administrators'`). Enforce **segregation of duties**, require approvals for group changes, and monitor/audit identity policy activity.
fields.remediation_cli: oci iam policy update --policy-id <example_resource_id> --statements "[\"Allow group <example_resource_name> to manage groups, users in tenancy where target.group.name != 'Administrators'\"]"
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Policies
2. Open any policy that allows a group to manage or use groups/users in the tenancy
3. Click Edit policy and update each affected statement to append exactly:
   where target.group.name != 'Administrators'
4. Save changes
5. Repeat for all such policies

fields.title: Identity Domain password policy expires passwords within 365 days
fields.remediation_text: Enforce **password rotation** at `<= 365` days in Identity Domains. Combine with **MFA**, strong composition rules, history, and minimum password age to prevent reuse. Apply **least privilege**, disable dormant accounts, and regularly review credential policies. *If on legacy IAM, adopt Identity Domains to gain expiration controls.*
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Identity & Security > Domains and select your identity domain
3. In the domain, open Security (or Domain settings) > Password policies
4. Edit the relevant password policy
5. Set "Password expires after (days)" to 365 or less
6. Click Save

fields.title: IAM password policy requires passwords to be at least 14 characters long
fields.remediation_text: Enforce a **minimum password length** of `>= 14`, preferably using passphrases. Combine with **MFA**, complexity and reuse limits, lockout/throttling, and routine policy reviews. Apply **least privilege** to limit blast radius and monitor authentication events. *If using external IdPs, require equivalent policies there.*
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Domains
2. Select <identity_domain_name> > Security > Password policy
3. Set Minimum length to 14 and click Save
4. If you do not use Identity Domains: go to Identity & Security > Authentication settings, edit Password policy, set Minimum password length to 14, and Save

fields.title: Identity Domain password policy prevents password reuse by remembering at least 24 previous passwords
fields.remediation_text: Enforce **password history** in Identity Domains with `num_passwords_in_history >= 24`. Pair with `min_password_age` to prevent rapid cycling, and maintain strong complexity and expiration rules. *If using legacy IAM, migrate to Identity Domains.* Complement with **MFA** for defense in depth.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Identity & Security > Domains and select <identity_domain_name>
3. Open Security > Password policies
4. Edit the affected policy (e.g., Default Password Policy)
5. Set "Number of passwords in history" (Remember previous passwords) to 24
6. Click Save
7. Repeat for any other password policies in the domain

fields.title: OCI IAM storage service-level admin policies exclude delete permissions
fields.remediation_text: Exclude delete permissions from storage service-level administrator policies. Use `request.permission!='VOLUME_DELETE'`, `request.permission!='VOLUME_BACKUP_DELETE'`, `request.permission!='FILE_SYSTEM_DELETE'`, `request.permission!='MOUNT_TARGET_DELETE'`, `request.permission!='EXPORT_SET_DELETE'`, `request.permission!='OBJECT_DELETE'`, and `request.permission!='BUCKET_DELETE'` as appropriate for each storage manage statement.
fields.remediation_cli: oci iam policy update --policy-id <policy-ocid> --statements "[\"Allow group VolumeUsers to manage volumes in tenancy where request.permission!='VOLUME_DELETE'\"]"
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Policies
2. Open each active policy that grants storage service-level administrators `manage` permissions
3. Edit storage manage statements to exclude the relevant delete permission with `request.permission`
4. Example: Allow group BucketUsers to manage buckets in tenancy where request.permission!='BUCKET_DELETE'
5. Save changes

fields.title: OCI IAM policy does not grant 'manage all-resources in tenancy' unless it is the Tenant Admin Policy
fields.remediation_text: Restrict `manage all-resources in tenancy` to the **Administrators** group only. Apply **least privilege** by scoping access to compartments and specific resource families, using conditions to narrow rights. Enforce **separation of duties**, maintain a *break-glass* admin model, and review policies regularly to prevent privilege drift.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Policies
2. Open each ACTIVE policy that is NOT named "Tenant Admin Policy"
3. Click Edit policy
4. Remove any statement containing: to manage all-resources in tenancy; or change it to: in compartment <compartment_name>
5. Click Save

fields.title: Tenancy administrator user has no API keys
fields.remediation_text: Do not issue **API keys** to tenancy administrators. Apply **least privilege** and **separation of duties**: use non-admin service accounts or principals with narrowly scoped rights and short-lived credentials. Require **SSO/MFA** for admin access, and enforce rapid key revocation and rotation for any programmatic identities.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the Oracle Cloud Console
2. Open the navigation menu and go to Identity & Security > Domains
3. Select your domain (<example_resource_name>), then click Users
4. Click the tenancy administrator user (<example_resource_name>)
5. Open the API Keys tab
6. For each API key, click Actions > Delete and confirm
7. Repeat until the API Keys list is empty

fields.title: User active API key is rotated within 90 days or less
fields.remediation_text:
Enforce **API key rotation** every `90` days.
- Issue a new key, confirm workloads use it, then revoke the old key
- Apply **least privilege** and avoid shared keys
- Limit active keys per user and remove unused ones
- Monitor usage and automate rotation for **defense in depth**
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Identity & Security > Users, then select the target user
3. Open API Keys and click Add API Key
4. Generate API Key Pair (or Upload/Paste Public Key), then click Add and download/copy the private key
5. For each API key older than 90 days, click the Actions (three dots) next to its fingerprint and select Delete
6. Confirm deletion

fields.title: User auth token age is 90 days or less
fields.remediation_text: Enforce routine **token rotation** at `<= 90 days` and prefer **short-lived, scoped credentials**. Apply **least privilege**, revoke unused tokens, set **automatic expirations**, and monitor usage. *When possible*, replace static tokens with federated or session-based access to reduce exposure.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Users
2. Open the user with the failing auth token
3. In the Auth Tokens tab, find tokens older than 90 days (check Created date)
4. Select the old token and click Delete
5. Confirm deletion
6. Repeat for any other tokens older than 90 days

fields.title: User customer secret key is rotated within 90 days or less
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Rotate **customer secret keys** every `<= 90` days. Apply **least privilege**, remove unused keys, and prefer short-lived identities (instance/resource principals) over static secrets. Automate rotation and alerts, avoid embedding keys in code, and continuously monitor key usage.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the Oracle Cloud Console
2. Go to Identity & Security > Domains > <example_resource_name> > Users > select <example_resource_name>
3. Open the Customer secret keys tab and click Generate secret key; save the Access Key and Secret
4. Delete any key older than 90 days: select the old key and click Delete

fields.title: User IAM database password was created within the last 90 days
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text:
Enforce rotation of **IAM database passwords** at or below `90 days` and expire old credentials. Automate issuance and revocation, and remove unused DB passwords.

Prefer **short-lived auth** (tokens or certificates) where supported, apply **least privilege** to DB roles, and monitor credential age to prevent drift.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Identity & Security > Domains and select your domain
3. Click Users and open the target user
4. In the user's page, open DB passwords (Database passwords)
5. Click Create DB password (or Reset) and confirm
6. Copy the generated password and update any services using it

fields.title: User with console password has MFA enabled for console access
fields.remediation_text: Require **MFA** for all users with Console passwords; prefer **phishing-resistant authenticators** (e.g., FIDO). Enforce via sign-on policies, prioritizing admins. Apply **least privilege**, disable Console passwords for service or federated users, and monitor auth logs to confirm ongoing MFA coverage.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Enable MFA (user action):
   - Sign in to the OCI Console as the affected user
   - Click your profile icon > User settings
   - Click "Enable Multi-Factor Authentication"
   - Scan the QR code with an authenticator app and enter the verification code, then click "Enable"
2. Or, remove console access (admin action) if the user doesn't need it:
   - In the Console, go to Identity & Security > Users
   - Open the user's page > Edit user capabilities
   - Uncheck "Can use Console password" and Save

fields.title: Integration Cloud instance uses a private endpoint or a public endpoint with IP or VCN allowlists
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Prefer **PRIVATE** endpoints and restrict access to specific VCNs. *If PUBLIC is required*, enforce strict IP allowlists-never `0.0.0.0/0`. Apply **least privilege** at network layers, place OIC behind **WAF/VPN**, segment with security lists, and monitor access logs. Review allowlists regularly as part of **defense in depth**.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Developer Services > Integration > Integration instances
2. Open <example_resource_name> and click Edit
3. If using Public endpoint: add an entry under Allowed IPs (e.g., <ALLOWED_CIDR>) and remove any 0.0.0.0/0
4. Alternatively, switch to Private endpoint if desired and select the required VCN/subnet
5. Click Save

fields.title: Customer-managed KMS key has rotation enabled with interval of 365 days or less
fields.remediation_text: Enable **automatic key rotation** and set an interval `<= 365` days (*shorter for sensitive data*). For vault types that do not support auto-rotation (e.g., External or Virtual Private vaults), **manually rotate** the key at least once every 365 days. Apply **least privilege** and **separation of duties** for key administration. Monitor rotation status, retire old key versions, and ensure applications handle key versioning to prevent outages.
fields.remediation_cli: oci kms management key update --key-id <example_resource_id> --endpoint <example_management_endpoint> --is-auto-rotation-enabled true --auto-key-rotation-details '{"rotationIntervalInDays": 365}'
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Vault
2. Open the vault, then under Resources select Master Encryption Keys
3. Click the target key name
4. For vaults that support auto-rotation: Click Edit auto-rotation settings, enable Auto rotation, set Rotation interval to 365 days (or less), and click Update
5. For vaults that do not support auto-rotation (e.g., External or Virtual Private vaults): Click 'Rotate Key' to manually rotate the key version at least once every 365 days

fields.title: Default security list restricts all traffic except ICMP within VCN
fields.remediation_text: Adopt a **deny-by-default** stance on the default list: allow only VCN-local `ICMP` for diagnostics. Use dedicated security lists or **network security groups** per application to explicitly allow needed ports and sources, and restrict egress to approved ranges. Review regularly under **least privilege**.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Networking > Virtual Cloud Networks and select your VCN
3. Open Security Lists and select the default security list
4. Click Edit All Rules
5. Remove all non-ICMP ingress and egress rules
6. Add an ingress rule: Protocol ICMP, Source <VCN_CIDR>
7. Add an egress rule: Protocol ICMP, Destination <VCN_CIDR>
8. Save changes

fields.title: Network security group restricts ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 3389 (RDP)
fields.remediation_text: Eliminate open `0.0.0.0/0` rules. Restrict **RDP** to trusted IPs and only when necessary. Prefer **private connectivity** via **VPN**, **bastion/jump hosts**, or **zero-trust** brokers. Apply **least privilege** and time-bound access, monitor logs, and disable RDP where unnecessary.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Networking > Network Security Groups
2. Open the <NSG_NAME>
3. Click Security Rules, then the Ingress tab
4. Find the rule with Source 0.0.0.0/0 and Protocol TCP (or All) allowing port 3389
5. Click Delete to remove the rule
   - If RDP is required, Edit instead and set Source to a specific CIDR (not 0.0.0.0/0)
6. Save changes

fields.title: Network security group restricts ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22 (SSH)
fields.remediation_text: Enforce **least privilege**: limit SSH in NSG rules to trusted CIDRs or private networks. Prefer **bastion access** (e.g., OCI Bastion) or **VPN/private connectivity** over direct Internet exposure. Use key-based auth, disable `PasswordAuthentication`, log and monitor access, and segment workloads for **defense in depth**.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Networking > Network Security Groups
2. Open the target NSG and go to the Rules tab
3. Find the INGRESS rule with Source 0.0.0.0/0 that includes TCP port 22
4. Click Remove to delete that rule
5. (If SSH is required) Add a new INGRESS rule for TCP port 22 with Source set to a specific trusted CIDR (not 0.0.0.0/0), then Save

fields.title: Security list restricts ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 3389 (RDP)
fields.remediation_text:
Block Internet access to RDP. 
- Deny `0.0.0.0/0` to `3389`; allow only trusted CIDRs.
- Prefer **private access** via a bastion, VPN, or zero-trust remote management.
- Enforce **least privilege** network rules, use **defense in depth**, and adopt *just-in-time* administrative access.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Networking > Virtual Cloud Networks and select your VCN
2. Under Resources, click Security Lists and open the list attached to the affected subnet
3. In Ingress Rules, locate any rule with Source CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 that allows TCP port 3389 or All Protocols
4. Delete that rule, or edit it so Source CIDR is a restricted range (e.g., your IP) and Destination Port is 3389 only
5. Click Save Changes

fields.title: Security list restricts ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22 (SSH)
fields.remediation_text: Restrict **SSH** to trusted sources using least-privilege network rules; avoid `0.0.0.0/0`. Prefer **private access** via VPN/peering or a hardened **bastion**. Apply **network segmentation** (NSGs/security lists) to narrow scope. Enforce **key-based authentication**, disable password login, and monitor access.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Networking > Virtual Cloud Networks and open your VCN
2. Click Security Lists, then select <example_resource_name>
3. In Ingress Rules, locate any rule with Source CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 and Protocol TCP (or All) that includes port 22
4. Edit the rule: change Source CIDR to a specific allowed range (e.g., your office IP/CIDR) and set Destination Port Range to 22, or delete the rule
5. Click Save changes

fields.title: Subnet has VCN flow logging enabled
fields.remediation_text: Enable **VCN flow logs** for all subnets-prefer VCN-wide enablement for complete coverage-and route to centralized log groups. Enforce least privilege on log access, set retention, and integrate with a SIEM. Use `capture filters` and `sampling` to control volume. Review logs to support defense-in-depth.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Networking > Flow logs
2. Click Enable flow logs
3. Select a Log group (or create one) and a Capture filter (or create one)
4. Click Next, then Add enablement points
5. Choose Virtual cloud network and select your VCN (or choose Subnet and select the subnet)
6. Click Add enablement points, then Next, then Enable flow logs

fields.title: Object Storage bucket is encrypted with a Customer Managed Key (CMK)
fields.remediation_text: Encrypt buckets with `CMEK`. Apply **least privilege** to key usage, enforce **separation of duties** between key and storage admins, mandate regular rotation, and monitor key access. Use **defense in depth** so encryption complements strict IAM and network controls rather than replacing them.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Storage > Object Storage & Archive Storage > Buckets
3. Open the target bucket
4. Click Edit bucket
5. Under Encryption, select Customer-managed key and choose the desired Vault key
6. Click Save

fields.title: Object Storage bucket has write-level logging enabled
fields.remediation_text:
Enable `write` service logs on all buckets and route them to a centralized log group for monitoring.

Apply **least privilege** to log data, enforce retention and immutability, and alert on anomalous write activity. Use **defense in depth** so bucket changes are accountable and swiftly detected.
fields.remediation_cli: oci logging log create --log-group-id <log-group-ocid> --display-name ObjectStorage-Write-Logs --log-type SERVICE --configuration '{"compartmentId":"<compartment-ocid>","source":{"service":"objectstorage","resource":"<bucket-name>","category":"write","sourceType":"OCISERVICE"}}'
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, select the target region and go to Observability & Management > Logging > Log groups
2. Open an existing log group or click Create log group
3. Click Create log
4. Type: Service
5. Service: Object Storage
6. Category: write
7. Resource: select the target bucket (bucket name must match)
8. Ensure Enabled is checked
9. Click Create

fields.title: Object Storage bucket is not publicly accessible
fields.remediation_text: Keep buckets **private** (`NoPublicAccess`) under the **least privilege** principle. For external sharing, use **pre-authenticated requests** or signed URLs with scoped permissions and expiry. Restrict access via IAM policies, enforce guardrails (*e.g.*, Security Zones), and regularly review bucket visibility.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Object Storage > Buckets and open <bucket-name>
3. Click Edit (Bucket details)
4. Set Public access type to "No public access"
5. Click Save

fields.title: Object Storage bucket has versioning enabled
fields.remediation_text: Enable **bucket versioning** (`Enabled`) for data that needs recovery. Apply **least privilege** to delete and overwrite actions, use **retention rules** or legal holds for critical data, and add **lifecycle policies** to manage older versions-providing **defense in depth** against destructive changes.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Storage > Buckets and open the target bucket
3. In Bucket details, find Versioning and click Edit
4. Select Enabled and click Save

fields.title: Tenancy admins are not used for routine operations
fields.remediation_text: Use least-privileged identities for routine work; reserve admins for approved break-glass.

fields.title: Tenancy-admin privileges are limited to the approved admin population
fields.remediation_text: Remove admin privileges from users outside the approved population.

fields.title: Public API gateways serve HTTPS only
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: No action required.

fields.title: Critical/high Cloud Guard problems are remediated within SLA
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Remediate or formally accept the problem.

fields.title: Cloud Guard problems are risk-classified
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Review Cloud Guard detector configuration.

fields.title: Storage resources are encrypted at rest
fields.remediation_text: No action required.

fields.title: OCI databases have automatic backups / point-in-time recovery
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Enable automatic backups in the database backup configuration.

fields.title: OCI databases are encrypted at rest
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: No action required; consider a customer-managed key.

fields.title: Mail domains publish DKIM records
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Publish the DKIM TXT/CNAME record supplied by the mail provider.

fields.title: Mail domains in OCI DNS publish SPF and DMARC
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Add TXT records 'v=spf1 ... -all' at the apex and 'v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; ...' at _dmarc.

fields.title: Public DNS zones have DNSSEC enabled
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Enable DNSSEC on the zone.

fields.title: Dynamic group matching rules are scoped
fields.remediation_text: Add a compartment or tag condition to the matching rule.

fields.title: No public (any-user) or cross-tenancy IAM grants
fields.remediation_text: Remove or scope the statement.

fields.title: IAM policies avoid any-user and wildcard administrator grants
fields.remediation_text: Replace the statement with least-privilege grants scoped to a compartment.

fields.title: No active IAM user is inactive for more than 90 days
fields.remediation_text: Disable or delete inactive users.

fields.title: Vault keys are enabled, rotating and owned
fields.remediation_text: Enable rotation and tag the key with an owner.

fields.title: Public load balancers expose HTTPS only
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Add an SSL configuration to listeners or replace HTTP listeners with an HTTPS redirect rule set.

fields.title: Load balancers have access/error logs enabled
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Enable access and error logs for the load balancer.

fields.title: Load balancer TLS listeners use TLS 1.2+ and modern ciphers
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Use a custom SSL cipher suite and protocols TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3 on every TLS listener.

fields.title: Log archive buckets are immutable (locked retention rule)
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Add a retention rule and lock it.

fields.title: Security logs are retained for at least 12 months
fields.remediation_text: Export logs through Service Connector Hub to a bucket with a >=365-day retention rule.

fields.title: Internet-facing VCNs have an OCI Network Firewall (IPS)
fields.remediation_text: Deploy an OCI Network Firewall with an IPS policy in the VCN's region.

fields.title: Database ports are not exposed to the internet
fields.remediation_text: Restrict database ingress to private CIDRs.

fields.title: No unapproved internet ingress in security lists / NSGs
fields.remediation_text: Restrict the source CIDR or remove the rule.

fields.title: Compute instances are registered and patched in OS Management Hub
fields.remediation_text: Register the instance and apply pending updates.

fields.title: Privileged users have MFA enabled
fields.remediation_text: Enable MFA for every privileged user.

fields.title: A tenancy-wide resource inventory can be produced
fields.remediation_text: Grant the assessment user inspect access via the Search service.

fields.title: Block and boot volumes have a backup policy assigned
fields.remediation_text: Assign a backup policy (bronze/silver/gold or a custom policy) to every volume.

fields.title: Host vulnerabilities are severity-classified
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Review unclassified findings.

fields.title: Compute instances are covered by a Vulnerability Scanning host scan target
fields.remediation_text: Create a host scan recipe and a host scan target covering the compartment of each instance.
fields.remediation_cli: oci vulnerability-scanning host scan target create --compartment-id <C> --host-scan-recipe-id <R> --target-compartment-id <C>

fields.title: Instances were vulnerability-scanned recently
fields.remediation_text: Schedule a recurring host scan recipe.

fields.title: Public load balancers are protected by an OCI WAF
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Create a WAF policy and a web application firewall for each public load balancer.

fields.title: Oracle Analytics Cloud instance is deployed within a Virtual Cloud Network or restricts public access to allowed sources
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Prefer **private deployment in a VCN** and apply **least privilege** network access. *If public is required*, enforce **allowlists** to specific IPs/CIDRs and never include `0.0.0.0/0`. Use **private access channels/service gateways**, require **MFA/SSO**, and apply **defense in depth** (WAF, audit monitoring) to reduce exposure.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Analytics & AI > Analytics Cloud and select your instance
2. On Instance Details, under Network Access, click Edit next to Access Control
3. Remove any 0.0.0.0/0 entry (if present)
4. Add an access rule with the specific allowed public IP or CIDR
5. Click Save

fields.title: Tenancy audit log retention period is 365 days or greater
fields.remediation_text:
Set audit retention to `>= 365` days at the tenancy level and protect the setting with **least privilege** and **separation of duties**.

Adopt **defense in depth**: export audit logs to centralized, immutable storage or a SIEM for extended retention, integrity, and continuous monitoring.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Open the OCI Console and go to Governance & Administration > Audit
2. Click Configuration
3. Set Retention period (days) to 365
4. Click Save

fields.title: Block volume is encrypted with a Customer Managed Key (CMK)
fields.remediation_text:
Use **Customer-Managed Keys** in Vault for all block volumes.
- Enforce least privilege and separation of duties on key usage
- Rotate keys regularly and monitor KMS events
- Validate that key disable/deny revokes data access
Apply the same controls to snapshots and backups.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Block Storage > Block Volumes
2. Open the failing volume
3. Click Edit
4. Under Encryption, select "Encrypt using customer-managed keys" and choose the vault key
5. Click Save changes

fields.title: Boot volume is encrypted with Customer Managed Key
fields.remediation_text: Encrypt boot volumes with **customer-managed keys** and enforce **least privilege** on key usage. Define a key lifecycle (new keys for rotation), monitor and audit key access, and restrict key scope to required compartments and services to achieve **defense in depth** and rapid revocation when needed.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Storage > Block Storage > Boot Volumes
2. Click the boot volume name
3. Click Edit (or Assign master encryption key)
4. Select a Customer-managed key from Vault
5. Click Save

fields.title: Cloud Guard is enabled in the root compartment of the tenancy
fields.remediation_text: Enable **Cloud Guard** at the tenancy root to centralize monitoring and automated response. Apply **defense in depth** by using detectors/responders, integrate alerts with monitoring, and enforce **least privilege** for its roles. Regularly tune policies and review findings to prevent blind spots.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Security > Cloud Guard
2. Ensure the root compartment is selected
3. Click Enable Cloud Guard
4. Choose a Reporting region
5. Click Enable

fields.title: Compute instance has in-transit encryption enabled
fields.remediation_text: Enable **in-transit encryption** for all paravirtualized volume attachments and make it standard in golden images and IaC. Apply **defense in depth** with **customer-managed keys** and regular rotation. Periodically verify attachments and remediate drift so no instance communicates with volumes over unencrypted channels.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Compute > Instances and open the target instance
2. Under Resources, click the boot volume attachment, choose Edit, enable "Use in-transit encryption", and Save
3. For each attached block volume (paravirtualized), open the attachment (More actions > Edit), enable "Use in-transit encryption", and Save
4. If Edit isn't available for an attachment, detach it and reattach it with "Use in-transit encryption" checked

fields.title: Compute instance legacy metadata service endpoint is disabled
fields.remediation_text: Disable **IMDS v1** and require **IMDS v2** across all instances. Migrate applications to session-authorized requests and confirm image support. Enforce **least privilege** for instance principals, restrict untrusted processes from reaching `169.254.169.254`, and monitor metadata access to provide **defense in depth**.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Compute > Instances
2. Select <example_resource_name>
3. In Instance Details, next to Instance metadata service, click Edit
4. Set Allowed IMDS version to Version 2 only
5. Click Save changes

fields.title: Compute instance has Secure Boot enabled
fields.remediation_text: Enable **Secure Boot** across instances and prefer **shielded instances**. Pair with **TPM** and **Measured Boot** where supported for defense in depth. Permit only trusted, signed kernels and drivers, and manage updates via hardened golden images and code signing. *On Windows VMs, use Secure Boot with TPM and Measured Boot.*
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Compute > Instances
2. Click Create instance
3. Choose an image and shape that support Shielded instance
4. In the Security section, click Edit under Shielded instance and enable Secure Boot
5. Click Create
6. To remove the failing resource, select the original non-shielded instance > More actions > Terminate

fields.title: Autonomous Shared Database (ADB) is deployed within a VCN or restricts public access with whitelisted IPs excluding 0.0.0.0/0
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text:
Prefer **VCN private endpoints** to eliminate internet exposure. If public access is required, enforce **least privilege** by limiting ACLs to specific CIDRs or VCNs; never use `0.0.0.0/0`.

Add **defense in depth** with NSGs and private connectivity (VPN/peering), monitor access, and rotate client wallets regularly.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Autonomous Database and select the instance
2. Click More Actions > Update
3. Under Network Access, enable Access control list (ACL)
4. Add an allowed IP/CIDR (exclude 0.0.0.0/0) and remove any 0.0.0.0/0 entry
5. Click Save

fields.title: Tenancy has at least one notification topic with active subscriptions
fields.remediation_text: Create a centralized **Notifications** topic with one or more **subscriptions**, and route critical Events/monitoring to it. Apply **least privilege** to topic management, use redundant channels, test delivery regularly, and tune filters to reduce noise. *Consider* escalation paths for `critical` alerts.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Menu > Application Integration > Notifications > Topics
2. Click Create Topic, enter a name, and click Create
3. Open the topic, click Create Subscription
4. Select a protocol (e.g., Function), choose/provide the endpoint, and click Create
5. Verify the subscription lifecycle state shows Active (confirm if prompted for protocols like Email)

fields.title: Event rule monitoring Cloud Guard problems has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Implement **event-driven alerts** for Cloud Guard problem lifecycle events and route them to trusted **notification channels** and your **SOC/SIEM**. Enforce **least privilege** on publish/subscribe, align rules with the **reporting region**, and use **severity-based filtering** to prioritize response within a **defense-in-depth** approach.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Menu > Application Integration > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create Rule and select the Compartment; switch to the Cloud Guard reporting Region
3. In Conditions, add event types: com.oraclecloud.cloudguard.problemdetected, com.oraclecloud.cloudguard.problemdismissed, com.oraclecloud.cloudguard.problemremediated
4. Under Actions, add Notifications and select the desired Topic
5. Ensure the rule is Enabled and click Create

fields.title: Event rule monitoring IAM group changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Create **Events rules** for IAM group `create`, `update`, and `delete` and route them to **Notifications** channels consumed by the SOC. Enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties** on rules/topics, forward events to a **SIEM**, and periodically test alert delivery.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule and set Name
3. In Condition, select Event types and add:
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.creategroup
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletegroup
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updategroup
4. In Actions, add Notifications and select an existing Topic
5. Click Create to save the rule

fields.title: Event rule monitoring IAM policy changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Create OCI Events rules for `...createpolicy`, `...updatepolicy`, and `...deletepolicy` with a **notification action** to trusted channels. Enforce **least privilege** on IAM and Events administration, require change approvals, and routinely test alerting to ensure rapid detection.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service
2. Click Create Rule and set Display Name (leave Enabled)
3. Under Conditions, choose Event Type, set Service Name to Identity and Access Management, and select:
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createpolicy
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deletepolicy
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updatepolicy
4. Under Actions, select Action Type: Notifications, then choose the target Topic
5. Click Create

fields.title: Event rule for identity provider changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Configure rules to capture **identity provider** `create`, `update`, and `delete` events and send notifications to responders and SIEM. Enforce **least privilege** on IdP management, require approvals for changes, and test alert paths. Use **defense in depth** with audit logging to spot anomalous identity changes.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules and click Create rule
2. Set Name and select the target Compartment
3. In Rule condition, add event types: CreateIdentityProvider, DeleteIdentityProvider, UpdateIdentityProvider (service: Identity)
4. In Actions, add Notification, select your Topic
5. Ensure Enabled is On and click Create

fields.title: Event rule for IdP group mapping changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Define **Events rules** for IdP group mapping changes (`com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.addidpgroupmapping`, `...removeidpgroupmapping`, `...updateidpgroupmapping`) and route notifications to monitored channels via **OCI Notifications**. Apply **least privilege** and **separation of duties**, and integrate alerts with a SIEM for **defense in depth**.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule
3. Condition: add Event types:
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.addidpgroupmapping
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.removeidpgroupmapping
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateidpgroupmapping
4. Actions: Add action > Notifications (ONS) and select the target Topic
5. Ensure Rule is Enabled and click Create

fields.title: Event rule monitoring local OCI user authentication has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Create an Events rule for `com.oraclecloud.identitysignon.interactivelogin` with **notification actions** delivering real-time alerts to monitored channels or workflows. Integrate with a SIEM, tune filters to reduce noise, and apply **least privilege** and **defense in depth** to limit local account exposure.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Application Integration > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule
3. Set Name and select the target Compartment
4. In Condition, set Event Type to: com.oraclecloud.identitysignon.interactivelogin
5. Add Action: choose Notifications, select the Topic, and ensure it is Enabled
6. Click Create

fields.title: Event rule monitoring network gateway changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text:
Define **event rules** that match `create`, `update`, `delete`, `attach`, and `detach` actions for all gateway types and send **notifications** to monitored channels.

Apply **least privilege** on topics, cover all compartments/regions, integrate with SIEM, and use **defense in depth** with network change approvals.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule and select the target Compartment
3. Set Display name
4. Under Matching events, add these Event types:
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createdrg
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletedrg
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatedrg
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createdrgattachment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletedrgattachment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatedrgattachment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changeinternetgatewaycompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createinternetgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deleteinternetgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updateinternetgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changelocalpeeringgatewaycompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createlocalpeeringgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletelocalpeeringgateway.end
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatelocalpeeringgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.natgateway.changenatgatewaycompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.natgateway.createnatgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.natgateway.deletenatgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.natgateway.updatenatgateway
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.attachserviceid
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.changeservicegatewaycompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.createservicegateway
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.deleteservicegateway.end
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.detachserviceid
   - com.oraclecloud.servicegateway.updateservicegateway
5. Add action: Notification, select the target Notifications (ONS) topic
6. Click Create (ensure the rule is enabled)

fields.title: Event rule monitoring network security group changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text:
Implement **Events** rules for NSG lifecycle changes with **notification actions** to a monitored topic/SIEM.
- Include `createnetworksecuritygroup`, `updatenetworksecuritygroup`, `deletenetworksecuritygroup`, `changenetworksecuritygroupcompartment`
- Enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties** on NSG and Events admins
- Regularly test and tune alerts
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule
3. Set Display name and Compartment
4. Under Conditions, add Event types:
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changenetworksecuritygroupcompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createnetworksecuritygroup
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletenetworksecuritygroup
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatenetworksecuritygroup
5. Under Actions, click Add action > Notifications, select Publish to topic, choose the ONS topic
6. Click Create to save the rule

fields.title: Event rule for route table changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Create an **Events rule** that captures route table `create`, `update`, `delete`, and `changeCompartment` events and routes them to **notifications** used by on-call and SIEM. Enforce **least privilege** on route edits, require **change approvals**, and apply **defense in depth** with auditing and automated response.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules.
2. Click Create rule and select the target Compartment; set a Display name.
3. In Condition, add event types:
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changeroutetablecompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createroutetable
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deleteroutetable
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updateroutetable
4. In Actions, add Notifications (ONS) and select the desired Topic.
5. Ensure the rule is Enabled and click Create.

fields.title: Event rule monitoring security list changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text: Define **Events** rules for security list create/update/delete and route them to **Notifications** or automated responders. Enforce **least privilege** for network and Events admins, apply **change control** with logging, cover critical compartments/regions, and periodically test alerts for reliability.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule, set a name and compartment
3. In Condition, set Event Type to include exactly:
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.changesecuritylistcompartment
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createsecuritylist
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletesecuritylist
   - com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatesecuritylist
4. Click Add action, choose Notifications, select an existing topic
5. Ensure the action is enabled and click Create

fields.title: Event rule monitoring user changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text:
Create and maintain **Events rules** for IAM user lifecycle changes and attach reliable **notification actions** to security-owned channels (SIEM, paging, email, chat).

Enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties** on rule management, and use **defense in depth** by correlating alerts with audit logs and automating containment.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In the OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules and click Create Rule
2. Select the Compartment and enter a Name
3. Under Rule Conditions, set Event Type to include:
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.createuser
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.deleteuser
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateuser
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateusercapabilities
   - com.oraclecloud.identitycontrolplane.updateuserstate
4. Under Actions, add a Notification action and select the desired Notifications (ONS) Topic
5. Click Create

fields.title: Event rule monitoring VCN changes has notification actions configured
fields.remediation_text:
Create and enable **Events rules** for VCN lifecycle changes (**create**, **update**, **delete**) with **notification actions** to monitored channels.

Apply **least privilege** to manage rules and notifications, integrate alerts with incident response, and periodically test to support **defense in depth**.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Observability & Management > Events Service > Rules
2. Click Create rule and enter a name; set Rule state to Enabled
3. Under Conditions, add Event types: com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.createvcn, com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.deletevcn, com.oraclecloud.virtualnetwork.updatevcn
4. Under Actions, add Notification and select the target Notifications topic
5. Click Create to save the rule

fields.title: File Storage file system is encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key
fields.message: No resources of the type evaluated by this check exist in the audited scope.
fields.remediation_text: Encrypt file systems with **Customer-Managed Keys** in OCI KMS. Apply **least privilege** on key usage, enable periodic rotation, and require dual control for key administration. Monitor key activity with centralized logging. Use **defense in depth** by combining `CMEK` with network isolation and strong access governance.
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Storage > File Storage > File Systems and select the target file system
3. In the Encryption section, click Edit (or Change key)
4. Select Customer-managed key, choose the Vault and KMS key
5. Click Save to apply

fields.title: All IAM policies granting manage/use on groups or users in the tenancy restrict access to the Administrators group
fields.remediation_text: Apply **least privilege**: avoid tenancy-wide manage/use on groups or users. When delegation is required, include a condition excluding the **Administrators** group (e.g., `target.group.name != 'Administrators'`). Enforce **segregation of duties**, require approvals for group changes, and monitor/audit identity policy activity.
fields.remediation_cli: oci iam policy update --policy-id <example_resource_id> --statements "[\"Allow group <example_resource_name> to manage groups, users in tenancy where target.group.name != 'Administrators'\"]"
fields.remediation_manual:
1. In OCI Console, go to Identity & Security > Policies
2. Open any policy that allows a group to manage or use groups/users in the tenancy
3. Click Edit policy and update each affected statement to append exactly:
   where target.group.name != 'Administrators'
4. Save changes
5. Repeat for all such policies

fields.title: Identity Domain password policy expires passwords within 365 days
fields.remediation_text: Enforce **password rotation** at `<= 365` days in Identity Domains. Combine with **MFA**, strong composition rules, history, and minimum password age to prevent reuse. Apply **least privilege**, disable dormant accounts, and regularly review credential policies. *If on legacy IAM, adopt Identity Domains to gain expiration controls.*
fields.remediation_manual:
1. Sign in to the OCI Console
2. Go to Identity & Security > Domains and select your identity domain
3. In the domain, open Security (or Domain settings) > Password policies
4. Edit the relevant password policy
5. Set "Password expires after (days)" to 365 or less
6. Click Save

fields.title: IAM password policy requires passwords to be at least 14 characters long
fields.remediation_text: Enforce a **minimum password length** of `>= 14`, preferably using passphrases. Combine with **MFA**, complexity and reuse limits, lockout/throttling, and routine policy reviews.
